classification.difficultyReason: Apply the taught equal-distance journey model, convert minutes to seconds, add the two half-journey times, and recover the full distance after solving.

content.prompt: Giorgia cycles to school every day. She manages to go half the distance at $4\text{ m/s}$ but slows to $3\text{ m/s}$ for the second half of her trip. She takes $35$ minutes to complete the trip. Find the distance she travels, to the nearest metre.

answer.short:
$7200\text{ m}$

Use time = distance ÷ speed for each half and add the two times.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ metres be half the distance. The times for the two halves are $\frac{x}{4}$ seconds and $\frac{x}{3}$ seconds. The total time is $35\times60=2100$ seconds.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{x}{4}+\frac{x}{3}&=2100\\3x+4x&=25200\\7x&=25200\\x&=3600\end{align*}$$

The full distance is $2\times3600=7200\text{ m}$, to the nearest metre.
